operatingSequences.condition: A public constituent-services dataset carried civic signal but was not yet a resident pathway.
operatingSequences.diagnosis: People needed issue-first entry points, district context, possible next steps, and source limitations without first interpreting the complete dataset.
operatingSequences.intervention: Jamie independently built a public prototype that translated administrative categories into issue-oriented guidance.
operatingSequences.coordination: He connected source data, information architecture, interface implementation, public documentation, and a bounded institutional-outreach layer.
operatingSequences.changedBehavior: A reader could enter through a recognizable concern, and issue pathways could be routed toward an intended Council-account audience.
operatingSequences.outcome: The prototype shipped publicly, received press and civic-data recognition, and has a documented eight-member Council-account authored-engagement floor.
boundaries: The intended 26-account audience is not reciprocal engagement.
CallNYC was independent, unofficial, and is not current guidance.
The record does not establish unique resident use or service outcomes.

operatingSequences.condition: A long-vacant historic building required preservation-sensitive stabilization and a neighborhood-led public-purpose process.
operatingSequences.diagnosis: Construction dependencies, specialist teams, municipal documentation, site conditions, and neighborhood knowledge needed one shared operating picture.
operatingSequences.intervention: Jamie co-founded and project-managed the effort, served as Phase One general contractor, and created a neighborhood survey and contact workflow.
operatingSequences.coordination: He connected masonry, roofing, framing, water, access, safety, consultants, measured drawings, survey cards, and daily field decisions.
operatingSequences.changedBehavior: Specialist work could be sequenced across the site while neighborhood conversations accumulated into a reusable planning record.
operatingSequences.outcome: Phase One produced a cold shell; the project received a CCED recommendation and Council appropriation; a separate recurring public-service interface also became visible.
boundaries: Specialist labor and public milestones remain collective.
The City appropriation was not disbursed to KC Town Hall.
The records do not establish that Jamie alone caused funding or performed every trade's work.

operatingSequences.project: NYC Artist Coalition and Commercial Rent Stabilization
operatingSequences.condition: Cultural-space and commercial-rent work crossed public policy, lived experience, legal questions, public data, meetings, and protected coalition context.
operatingSequences.diagnosis: Without shared memory and translation infrastructure, decisions, sources, follow-up, and public/private boundaries fragmented.
operatingSequences.intervention: Jamie helped establish recurring participation infrastructure and built campaign-memory, source-map, public-data, and policy-communication systems.
operatingSequences.coordination: The work connected rotating cultural-space meetings, stakeholder follow-up, testimony, campaign sites, decision records, source lineages, and review lanes.
operatingSequences.changedBehavior: Collaborators could orient after meetings, find source context, track next steps, prepare testimony, and distinguish public explanation from protected strategy.
operatingSequences.outcome: Official records document coalition formation and testimony; public campaigns contributed to nightlife-policy and cultural-space debates; current CRS work has reusable memory and provenance infrastructure.
boundaries: Government outcomes and coalition work remain collective.
The record does not assign Jamie sole causation for laws, offices, or agency change.
Private strategy, legal-review material, and stakeholder records remain protected.
